title: Per-tenant token-aware SLI schema and soft-circuit playbook for graceful degradation
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define and implement a per-endpoint / per-model SLI schema that is token-aware and tenant-weighted, plus an operational playbook for soft circuit breakers and prioritized load shedding across regions. Purpose: reduce cascading outages during token-heavy spikes while preserving high-priority customer traffic and model quality. This ticket covers SLI definitions, error-budget burn rules, cross-region escrow/borrowing, soft-circuit behavior, metrics instrumentation, dashboards, and a staged rollout plan.
background: Recent incidents revealed that token-volume spikes (long LLM completions) cause disproportionate tail-latency and error bursts. Existing endpoint SLOs are not token-normalized and lack tenant prioritization, causing small high-value customers to suffer during global bursts. We need SLIs that reflect real cost/latency drivers (token count, KV hit ratio) and a graceful, observable degradation strategy that can be automated and audited.
sli_definitions: 1) Token-normalized success rate: percentage of requests that complete without 5xx or model-fallback after normalizing for token_count (weighted by tokens). 2) Latency p95 token-normalized: p95 of (latency / sqrt(token_count+1)) aggregated per-route and per-tenant. 3) Tail-latency p99: raw p99 for short-form routes (<=128 tokens) and for long-form routes (>512 tokens) separately. 4) Quality SLI: promptset-based pass-rate for sampled requests per model-variant measured by embedding similarity threshold. 5) KV cache hit ratio: fraction of requests benefiting from prefix/KV cache. 6) Fallback ratio: % of requests that required fallback to lower-cost variant or remote region. Metrics must be emitted with dimensions: tenant_id, route_id, model, variant, region, token_count_bucket. All metrics names prefixed with redwood.sli.*
error_budget_policy: Error budgets are computed per (tenant, route, model) on a rolling 30-day window. Budgets are token-weighted: error_budget_tokens = allowed_error_rate * observed_token_volume. Burn rate calculation: (errors_tokens / error_budget_tokens) over sliding 1h and 6h windows. Thresholds: - Green: burn_rate < 1 -> normal operations. - Yellow: 1 <= burn_rate < 4 -> automate mitigations (reduce default max_tokens for new requests on that route, enable cache priming). - Red: burn_rate >= 4 -> engage soft-circuit: prioritize traffic, enact pre-configured degradation for affected tenant-route-model sets, and page on-call. Error budget borrowing: regions can loan up to 10% of their error budget to another region for a given tenant via escrow tickets; borrowing eats into the lender's next 7-day budget and is recorded in metrics and audit logs.
soft_circuit_behaviour: Soft circuit breakers operate at three scopes: model-variant level, route-level, and tenant-level. They are 'soft' because they transition through degradations rather than hard rejects: 1) First-stage (adaptive admission): reduce acceptance of requests that exceed per-req token threshold by returning 429 with Retry-After or auto-trim prompt using a configurable trimming policy. 2) Second-stage (variant degrade): preferentially route to smaller/quantized variants with model-specific quality delta guardrails; stream partial text responses if available. 3) Third-stage (priority shedding): drop non-paid/free-tier and best-effort traffic preemptively, preserve enterprise SLAs and pinned variants. All stages log a causality id, previous variant id, and decision signal to be surfaced in request trace.
load_shedding_rules: - Token budget windowing: maintain per-tenant token_budget_per_minute derived from committed throughput or usage history. - Long-tail backpressure: for any route where >20% of active requests are >75th token_size percentile for that route, apply admission control. - Cache-first: if KV cache_hitrate < 0.3 and route has high reuse, enable aggressive cache-priming for top prefixes. - Queueing limits: per-region soft-queue depth with oldest-request-first eviction for low-priority tenants. - Fallback routing: if region is overloaded, try local variant fallback; if unsuccessful, route to secondary region respecting tenant data residency tags. - Observability gating: shedding actions must be accompanied by metrics emits and a Console event within 30s.
instrumentation_requirements: 1) New metrics: redwood.sli.token_success_tokens, redwood.sli.token_errors_tokens, redwood.sli.sli_burn_rate_1h, redwood.sli.sli_burn_rate_6h, redwood.sli.escrow_borrowed_tokens, redwood.sli.soft_circuit_state, redwood.sli.degradation_reason. 2) Dimensions: tenant_id, route_id, model, variant, region, instance_pool. 3) Traces: attach circuit_decision and variant_swap metadata to request traces. 4) Logs: structured events for every degradation decision with request_id, tenant_id, cause, and prior metrics snapshot. 5) Sampling: quality SLI sampling must capture full prompt/response for 0.1% of requests, routed to secure audit storage for 90 days.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: - Per-tenant SLI overview with token-normalized availability and burn-rate histogram. - Heatmap: region x route error budget utilization. - Degradation timeline for each active soft-circuit. Alerts: - burn_rate_1h > 2 for >15m -> Pager (on-call reliability). - burn_rate_6h > 1.5 for >1h -> Email + Slack channel. - soft_circuit_state == 'engaged' for critical tenants -> Pager. Alerts include contextual links: top offending routes, top tenants, recent canary metrics. All alerts must link to runbook and to Console run-time snapshot.
runbook_highlevel: 1) Detect: alarm triggers showing burn rate or sudden token surge. 2) Triage: on-call inspects per-tenant token distribution and KV hit ratios. 3) Mitigate: enable soft-circuit stage 1 via playbook UI for the affected route(s), adjust max_tokens for new requests, and prime KV cache. 4) Escalate: if stage 1 ineffective within 10 minutes escalate to stage 2 (variant degrade) and notify product and support to prepare customer comms. 5) Recover: gradually lift degradations in reverse order after burn_rate falls below 0.8 for 2 successive 15m windows. 6) Postmortem: create incident doc with burned token accounting and propose quota or product changes to prevent recurrence.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary, 2 weeks): implement metrics, soft-circuit feature-flagged, 5% of traffic across non-critical routes; validate emits and dashboarding. Phase B (staged expansion, 3 weeks): enable for 25% traffic, run chaos tests (region ejection) in staging and run bounded faults in prod during low-traffic windows. Phase C (tenant opt-in, 2 weeks): enable for enterprise tenants with config controls in Console (priority tiers, per-tenant trimming rules). Phase D (global enable): after 4-week stability window and sign-off from SRE, enable default policies globally and remove feature flags. All phases require a pre-flight checklist and an SLI gating report signed by SRE and Product.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All new metrics are emitted and visible in Console dashboards. 2) Canaries demonstrate no >10% QoL regression for pinned enterprise tenants during simulated token spikes. 3) Automated gating: deploy pipeline blocks if burn_rate_6h > 2 in canary environment. 4) Runbook validated in a simulated incident (chaos test) with on-call able to perform mitigation steps within SLA. 5) Post-deploy audit: token-level error accounting is queryable for last 90 days.
testing_plan: - Load tests: synthetic workloads mimicking long-form completions with 5k concurrent sessions across two regions, verifying per-tenant quotas and shedding behavior. - Chaos engineering: region ejection, network partition between control plane and region, instance pool evictions. - Quality regression: run promptset evaluation before/after variant degrade for top 10 enterprise tenants. - UI/Console tests: feature flag toggles, per-tenant configuration saved and audited. - Security review: sampling and storage of prompts must pass data retention policy checks.
implementation_notes: - Backend: extend admission controller to be token-aware and tenant-scoped. - Runtime: add soft-circuit operator in routing layer that can mutate routing rules at request-time with minimal latency. - Storage: escrow ledger persisted to central DB with per-region replication and audit trail. - DB schema: tenant_token_budgets (tenant_id, minute_bucket, tokens_used, borrowed_from). - Backwards compatibility: default to current SLO behavior when flags disabled. - Performance: ensure extra metric emission adds <2ms to request tail.
security_and_privacy: Quality sampling stores prompts/responses for 90 days in encrypted audit storage (KMS). Sampling only active on accounts with data-retention consent; privacy team to approve sampling policy. All logs with PII redaction; token_level metrics are aggregated and do not include raw text except in sampled records.
outstanding_risks_and_open_questions: 1) How to quantify quality degradation bounds when switching to quantized variants across different model families? 2) Does borrowing across regions violate any data residency commitments for certain tenants? (Legal to confirm). 3) Risk of oscillation: repeated engage/disengage could thrash caches—need hysteresis parameters. 4) Telemetry volume: token-weighted metrics may increase cardinality; evaluate storage costs.
next_steps: 1) Run SLI definition review with Product and Research (Priya Patel, Liam O'Connor) by 2025-02-20. 2) Implement metrics scaffolding and create dashboard mocks (ENG-887902) in Cycle 2025-W10. 3) Build canary admission controller feature flag and run canary on non-critical routes. 4) Legal/privacy sign-off on sampling policy. 5) Schedule chaos tests and pre-flight checklist for Phase B.
